subtitles.zh: 今天看出口增长，中国超过20%，台湾超过40%，韩国接近60%。

subtitles.en: But when you look at domestic response, what we found is Taiwan sees the biggest reaction, followed by Korea. The impact in China is way less notable.
subtitles.zh: 但看国内反应，我们发现台湾反应最大，其次是韩国。中国的影响则明显小得多。

subtitles.en: Partially because a lot of that gain has been offset by domestic headwinds. Why that matters is because this diverging reaction has really important and different implications for fiscal and monetary policy in each economy.
subtitles.zh: 部分因为很多收益被国内逆风抵消。这之所以重要，是因为这种分化的反应对各经济体的财政和货币政策有重要且不同的含义。

subtitles.en: To understand from our economics perspective, you really had to see what is the impact for the actual domestic spillover. When we say domestic spillover, we're really talking about two channels: one is capex, one is consumer spending.
subtitles.zh: 从经济学角度看，关键要看对国内传导的实际影响。我们说的国内传导，其实有两个渠道：一是资本开支，二是消费支出。

subtitles.en: Capex tends to be more reactive, for a bigger degree, because profitable companies can easily turn their earnings into capacity to develop new factories and equipment. Why we think Korea and Taiwan stand out is because they have three things working in favor of them.
subtitles.zh: 资本开支往往反应更大，因为盈利企业容易把利润转化为产能，开发新工厂和设备。我们认为韩国和台湾突出，是因为有三点优势。

subtitles.en: One is they have a large enough tech sector relative to the overall economy. AI-exposed exports account for nearly 70% of nominal GDP in Taiwan and around 20% in Korea. So when you get that boost, you easily generate a bigger impulse. What's that share for China? It's only 5%.
subtitles.zh: 一是科技部门相对整体经济足够大。AI相关出口占台湾名义GDP近70%，韩国约20%。所以获得提振时，更容易产生更大推力。中国这一比例呢？只有5%。

subtitles.en: Besides that, Korea and Taiwan also have tight capacity. When you have additional demand, you can easily get new expansion. Whereas in China, additional demand from external sources is lifting utilization rates from previously falling levels, but it's not yet at the level that you can generate additional expansion.
subtitles.zh: 此外，韩国和台湾产能偏紧。有额外需求时，容易形成新扩张。而在中国，外部额外需求正把产能利用率从之前下滑的水平拉高，但还没到能产生额外扩张的程度。

subtitles.en: On top of that, the broader investment impulse in China is also influenced by other factors: weak demand, local government funding pressures, and a property downturn that's still weighing on overall investment.
subtitles.zh: 此外，中国更广泛的资本开支推力还受其他因素影响：需求偏弱、地方政府资金压力，以及地产调整仍在拖累整体资本开支。

subtitles.en: There are a lot of similarities. Besides capex, we're also seeing consumer spillover in both economies. If you look at retail sales on a three-month average basis, Taiwan is seeing retail sales at around 8% year over year. Korea was higher in the middle of the year at 6%, now is around 4%.
subtitles.zh: 有很多相似之处。除了资本开支，两个经济体也看到消费传导。看三个月平均零售销售，台湾同比约8%。韩国年中更高达6%，现在约4%。

subtitles.en: So definitely you're seeing that spillover both into corporate capex and consumer spending. But what is interesting is that you're seeing very different reaction in terms of monetary policy in these two economies. The Bank of Korea already raised twice.
subtitles.zh: 所以确实看到传导到企业资本开支和消费支出。但有趣的是，两个经济体的货币政策反应非常不同。韩国央行已经加息两次。

subtitles.en: And we're expecting them to continue with interest rate hikes two more times for the next six months. That's on top of echoing what you're saying: you're seeing not just the tech boom, but it's increasingly spilling to overall economic growth.
subtitles.zh: 我们预计未来六个月他们还会再加息两次。这呼应了你的说法：不仅是科技繁荣，而且正越来越多传导到整体经济增长。

subtitles.en: The case with Taiwan is interesting because despite our finding that they have more domestic spillover, the Taiwan CBC was on hold in September. So what we think that means is that the case for further monetary tightening in Taiwan is also getting stronger. As a result, we do expect the CBC to move forward with a rate hike in their upcoming December monetary meeting.
subtitles.zh: 台湾的情况有趣，尽管我们发现其国内传导更多，但台湾央行9月按兵不动。我们认为这意味着台湾进一步收紧货币政策的理由也在增强。因此，我们预计台湾央行将在12月会议上加息。

subtitles.en: The case with China is that even though they have a very similar external impulse, the impact to capex, as I mentioned, is weaker. The impact on consumer is even less. For example, the share of employment that works in relevant tech manufacturing accounts for less than two percent of total employment in China.
subtitles.zh: 中国的情况是，尽管外部推力非常相似，但正如我提到的，对资本开支的影响较弱。对消费的影响更小。例如，相关科技制造业就业占总就业不到2%。

subtitles.en: Just given how massive and diverse the economy is, that feed-through is also more limited on the consumer side. In China, there's a continued drag from the housing downturn. In terms of household wealth effect, you're still seeing decline, and wage expectations are still weak.
subtitles.zh: 鉴于经济规模庞大且多元，对消费端的传导也更有限。在中国，地产调整持续拖累。就家庭财富效应而言，仍在下降，工资预期也仍偏弱。

subtitles.en: On top of that, in Taiwan and Korea, one interesting observation is that because of this tech boom, you're seeing higher fiscal revenue, and that is in turn feeding into the broader economy, adding further impulse. In China, you're also seeing higher fiscal revenue from these corporate taxes, but it hasn't translated into higher fiscal spending.
subtitles.zh: 此外，在台湾和韩国，一个有趣观察是，由于科技繁荣，财政收入更高，这反过来又传导到更广泛经济，增添进一步推力。在中国，企业税收也带来更高财政收入，但尚未转化为更高的财政支出。

subtitles.en: In part because local government is still constrained by their overall funding condition. With that said, we do think China should maintain a more easing bias. For the PBOC, we don't have any rate cut expectations in the near horizon, but we are seeing they're doing incremental measures to help cushion the downside.
subtitles.zh: 部分因为地方政府仍受整体资金状况约束。尽管如此，我们认为中国应保持更偏宽松的倾向。对央行，我们短期内没有降息预期，但看到他们正采取增量措施帮助缓冲下行压力。

subtitles.en: Just a few weeks ago, right before the Golden Week holiday, you did see PBOC come out with more supportive measures, targeted for housing subsidies for example. Going forward, we do think export growth is a really important indicator to watch. Should we see more meaningful slowing on that front, we do think policymakers will come out more proactively and engage with more both fiscal and monetary easing.
subtitles.zh: 就在几周前，国庆假期前，确实看到央行出台更多支持措施，例如针对住房补贴。展望未来，我们认为出口增长是非常重要的观察指标。如果看到出口明显放缓，我们认为政策制定者会更主动出手，推出更多财政和货币宽松。

subtitles.en: I do think this is definitely a double-edged sword, especially the volatility in financial markets recently reminds us that what can drive up domestic demand can be the very same channels that deepen a downturn in the future.
subtitles.zh: 我确实认为这绝对是双刃剑，尤其是近期金融市场波动提醒我们，推高国内需求的渠道，未来也可能加深下行。

subtitles.en: So we do think that Korea and Taiwan, because of the strong reliance on this entire AI cycle and exports, make them more vulnerable than in the case with China. And the case with China is already a more diverse economy, it's bigger, so any potential shock will be more manageable.
subtitles.zh: 我们认为韩国和台湾由于高度依赖整个AI周期和出口，比中国更脆弱。而中国经济更加多元、规模更大，所以任何潜在冲击都更可控。

subtitles.en: At the same time, because Chinese policymakers haven't really done much in terms of rolling out stimulus, as I mentioned earlier, should there be any potential negative shock, we also think Chinese policymakers will act more proactively and come up with additional policy measures to rescue any potential shock.
subtitles.zh: 同时，由于中国政策制定者在推出刺激方面尚未大动作，正如我早先提到，如果出现任何潜在负面冲击，我们也认为中国政策制定者会更主动行动，推出额外政策措施来应对潜在冲击。

具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
把 Bloomberg LP 等来源或公司法律后缀误当成采访对象
没有公开证据却暗示嘉宾撒谎、操纵或言行不一
